claims.text: The starting material is an equiatomic or near-equiatomic CoCrFeNiTi elemental powder mixture.
CoCrFeNiTi before severe deformation typically has a micrometer-scale, single-phase FCC structure.
Approximately 6 hours of high-energy ball milling will produce severe lattice strain in CoCrFeNiTi.
Approximately 6 hours of high-energy ball milling will refine the CoCrFeNiTi grains to below 100 nm.
Milling-induced lattice strain and grain refinement lower the activation-energy barrier for an FCC-to-BCC solid-solution transition.
The VEC and atomic-radius mismatch introduced by Ti govern the stability of the proposed FCC-to-BCC transition.
SPS at 1000°C activates diffusion pathways in the strained powder and produces greater than 98% theoretical density.
A 10-minute SPS treatment at 1000°C is below the threshold for excessive grain coarsening and Ti-driven HCP precipitation.
The processed alloy will have a nanocrystalline, predominantly BCC or FCC/BCC dual-phase matrix with negligible porosity and no detectable HCP Laves phase.
Grain-boundary strengthening and solid-solution hardening will enhance the hardness of the processed alloy.
The processed CoCrFeNiTi alloy will have a Vickers hardness of 450–600 HV, compared with approximately 200–300 HV for cast CoCrFeNiTi.
The processed alloy will have a yield strength above 800 MPa.
Cast CoCrFeNiTi typically has an FCC single-phase structure, hardness of approximately 200–300 HV, and casting-related porosity.
SPS above 1050°C or with a dwell longer than 20 minutes causes excessive grain growth and/or Ti-rich HCP precipitation, reducing ductility and potentially causing embrittlement.
Milling for less than 4 hours produces insufficient lattice strain for the FCC-to-BCC transition and therefore retains a lower-hardness FCC structure.
The critical milling duration is expected to lie between 5 and 7 hours and to depend on mill energy input.
The HCP-precipitation threshold depends on Ti content and local stoichiometric variation.
HEBM followed by SPS can produce high-hardness BCC-containing high-entropy alloys.
Extended processing of Nb-doped CoCrFeNi analogs produces brittle HCP or Laves-like phases.
Vickers hardness testing at a 100 g load isolates grain-boundary strengthening from precipitation hardening.

contradictions.description: The starting state is described simultaneously as an elemental powder mixture and as an as-cast, single-phase FCC alloy. A pre-mixed collection of elemental powders is not the same initial structural state as an already alloyed, as-cast FCC material.
